title: Build a YouTube channel profile
summary: Set up a channel that says clearly who it is for and why to watch. This is about the profile and the system behind it, not a promise of views or income.
audience: Anyone who wants a channel people can understand in five seconds.
disclaimer: Education only. Nobody can promise audience growth or earnings. Follow YouTube's own policies, disclose sponsorships and respect copyright.

modules.title: Identity
modules.goal: A channel whose purpose is obvious from its name, banner and description.

steps.title: Decide who it is for and what they get
steps.why: Channels that try to speak to everyone usually speak to no one. One audience and one promise makes every later choice easier.
do: Write one sentence: 'I help <who> do <what> so they can <result>'.
List three video ideas that fit that sentence and three that do not.

prompts.label: Sharpen the promise
prompts.text: Here is my channel idea: <idea>. Ask me five questions that would make the audience and promise more specific, then propose three versions of the one-sentence promise.

tips: If you cannot say who it is not for, it is too broad.
Pick something you can make fifty videos about.
steps.check: You have a one-sentence promise and a list of ideas that fit it.

steps.title: Pick a name and handle that match everywhere
steps.why: People find you by search and by memory. The same short name across your channel, handle and other profiles builds recognition.
do: Brainstorm ten names, cross out hard-to-spell and hard-to-say ones.
Check the handle is free on the platforms you plan to use before you commit.

prompts.label: Name ideas
prompts.text: Suggest 15 short, easy-to-say channel names for: <promise sentence>. Avoid trademarks and avoid names that need explaining.

tips: Say it out loud: if you stumble, so will they.
Do not copy a larger creator's name.
steps.check: You chose one name and confirmed the handle is available.

steps.title: Write the About section and plan the banner
steps.why: The About section and banner are your shop window. They should answer: what is this, who is it for, when do new videos come.
do: Write the first two lines of the About so they work even if the rest is cut off.
Sketch the banner: name, promise, upload rhythm, and nothing else.

prompts.label: Draft the About
prompts.text: Write a channel About section (under 150 words) for: <promise>. First two lines must state who it is for and what they get. Add the upload schedule: <schedule>. Honest tone, no hype, no income claims.

commands.label: Make a banner concept
commands.text: Make a channel banner: dark background, the name <name> in bold, the tagline <promise>, a simple shape on the right.
commands.where: NEXXUS command bar, in Creation mode

tips: Put contact or business email in the dedicated field, not in the banner.
Use a banner that reads well on a phone, where it is cropped.
steps.check: Your About and a banner concept are written down.

modules.title: The weekly system
modules.goal: A simple routine you can keep up.

steps.title: Script a 60-second channel trailer
steps.why: The trailer is what a new visitor sees first. It should say who the channel is for, show a taste, and tell them what to expect.
do: Write a script with a hook, the promise, one example and a clear invitation.
Record it and watch it with the sound off: does it still make sense?

prompts.label: Trailer script
prompts.text: Write a 60-second channel trailer script for <promise>. Structure: 5-second hook, the promise, one concrete example, what to expect and when, one-line invitation. Plain language, spoken style.

tips: Lead with what the viewer gets, not who you are.
Add captions: many people watch muted.
steps.check: You have a trailer script written.

steps.title: Make titles and thumbnails a repeatable habit
steps.why: A title and thumbnail are a promise about the video. Keep the promise honest and make it quick to understand.
do: For your next video write five titles and sketch two thumbnail ideas.
Pick the one that is clearest, not the cleverest.

prompts.label: Title options
prompts.text: Give me ten honest title options for a video about <topic> for <audience>. No clickbait, no all-caps, each under 60 characters, each promising something the video really delivers.

commands.label: Thumbnail concept
commands.text: Make a thumbnail concept: big readable text '<three words>', one clear subject, high contrast.
commands.where: NEXXUS command bar, in Creation mode

tips: If the thumbnail needs a paragraph to explain, simplify it.
Never promise what the video does not show.
steps.check: You have five titles and two thumbnail ideas for one video.

steps.title: Set a weekly review
steps.why: Improvement comes from looking at what happened and changing one thing. A fixed weekly slot makes it automatic.
do: Each week write: what worked, what did not, and one change for next week.

prompts.label: Review template
prompts.text: Here are my channel numbers this week: <numbers>. Help me find one thing that worked, one that did not, and the single change most worth testing next week. Do not draw big conclusions from small numbers.

tips: Small samples lie. Look for patterns over several videos.
Change one thing at a time so you can tell what helped.
steps.check: Your weekly review slot and template exist.
